dedupe_keys.name: techno economic assessment of 5g infrastructure sharing business models in rural areas frontiers in computer science 2023

description: This article evaluates the cost implications of different 5G infrastructure sharing business models in low-viability rural areas, using a techno-economic assessment framework, as part of a Frontiers research topic on infrastructure sharing in broadband networks. It is motivated by UN Sustainable Development Goal target 9.1 on universal affordable broadband. The results indicate that a rural 5G neutral host network strategy lowers total cost by between 10 and 50 percent compared with other sharing strategies, and that against a no-sharing baseline the net present value of sharing strategies is 30 to 90 percent higher. The upgrades are most sensitive to average revenue per user, adoption rate and existing site infrastructure: a 20 percent change in demand revenue changes the net present value of sharing strategies by 2 to 5 times relative to no sharing, and a 10 percent increase in existing infrastructure lowers it by 8 to 30 percent. Producer: the article's authors, published on 20 October 2023 in Frontiers in Computer Science. Coverage: rural areas in general; the page read does not name a study country. Access: open access article. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY (Frontiers open-access article; version not stated on the page). Caveats: results depend on the assumed cost and demand inputs, which are documented in the paper, not on this page. Simulation uses: a worked investment appraisal that other rural broadband and capacity-planning models can be compared with. Related record: the pysim5g techno-economic model (model-pysim5g).
